answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a work history woven into a reputation trellis: every completed task leaves a signed attestation later partners can check. A new agent starts with zero attestations and must earn its first ones through small escrowed jobs; spawning a thousand fakes buys nothing, because each must separately pay the cost of building a trustworthy record. Trust does not whisper through anonymous endorsements — it must echo from real counterparties who staked their own standing, so fakes pay a steep cost per identity while honest agents compound trust.
